newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND FRONT ROW FACE TESTING TIMES.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND FRONT ROW FACE TESTING TIMES.

text.p: England's Triple Crown winning front row have been given a final chance to pip their Celtic tour colleagues for a British Lions test place in a final warm-up against the Emerging Springboks in Wellington on Tuesday.
Props Jason Leonard and Graham Rowntree have been named with hooker Mark Regan in what amounts to a last chance to sway the selectors' thinking before Saturday's opening test in Cape Town.
"Everyone will see this as a final trial. It will be a chance for them to stake a claim to a test place," said manager Fran Cotton.
He added it was "completely incorrect" to assume that the 15 players on show had already been ruled out of contention for Saturday's showdown with South Africa.
"We said even before the Natal game on Saturday that in these last two games we would give every player a fair opportunity to force their way in," added Cotton.
The Lions will pick their test side on Tuesday evening but will not officially announce it until just before kick-off. They will train behind closed doors for the rest off the week.
The English front row appeared to have been overtaken in the race for a test place by the Welsh, Irish and Scottish combination of David Young, Keith Wood and Tom Smith.
Leonard, who will captain the Lions for the second time on tour, said: "I don't think I will need to say a lot to the guys beforehand as everyone will be very geared up to perform.
"Speaking personally I would say there's more to come but we have all aimed to peak for the tests."
Tony Diprose, called out as a replacement for the injured number eight Scott Quinnell, makes his first appearance on tour.
His Saracens teammate Kyran Bracken, a replacement for injured Rob Howley, was due to arrive on Tuesday morning.

British Lions - 15-Tim Stimpson, 14-John Bentley, 13-Allan Bateman, 12-Will Greenwood, 11-Nick Beal, 10-Mike Catt, 9-Austin Healey, 8-Tony Diprose, 7-Neil Back, 6-Rob Wainwright, 5-Jeremy Davidson, 4-Nigel Redman, 3-Jason Leonard, 2-Mark Regan, 1-Graham Rowntree.
